module: packages/shared/src/regex.ts (SillyTavern regex-script engine: placement gate, slash-regex parser, replacement syntax, trim filter, depth window)
summary: Decides whether a stored regex script runs for a given placement/context (disabled, markdown-vs-prompt three-way gate, isEdit/runOnEdit, min/max depth window, placement membership) and, when it does, how `/pattern/flags` is parsed and how `$N` / `$<name>` / `{{match}}` are expanded — with capture values passed through the trim-string filter and the whole replacement macro-substituted last.

behaviours.rule: parseRegexFromString requires the WHOLE string to be delimited: the regex is anchored `^\/([\w\W]+?)\/([gimsuy]*)$`. The pattern group is lazy `+?` (so at least one char — an empty pattern `//` does not parse) and the flags group only admits the exact set `gimsuy`. Anything else — `/a/d`, `/a/v`, `/a/gg`, `/a/0`, leading or trailing space, a trailing newline — returns null.
behaviours.pinnedBy: packages/shared/src/regex.test.ts:32 (parses a delimited pattern and its flags); packages/shared/src/regex.test.ts:48 (rejects text that is not delimited and patterns that do not compile — only covers the bare word 'dragon')

behaviours.rule: A second guard rejects the string when the captured pattern contains a `/` that is NOT immediately preceded by a backslash: `pattern.match(/(^|[^\\])\//)` → null. A slash at the very start of the pattern counts as unescaped. This guard exists because `new RegExp('a/b')` compiles fine, so without it `/a/b/i` would parse with pattern `a/b` rather than going to the flags branch.
behaviours.pinnedBy: packages/shared/src/regex.test.ts:44 (rejects an unescaped delimiter inside the pattern); packages/shared/src/regex.test.ts:40 (unescapes an escaped delimiter inside the pattern)

behaviours.rule: The pre-backslash test is purely one-character lookback, so a `/` preceded by `\\` (an escaped backslash, i.e. two backslashes) is also accepted, even though it is not escaped. `/a\\/b/` parses to source `a\/b`.
behaviours.pinnedBy: NONE

behaviours.rule: Exactly ONE `\/` → `/` unescape is performed (`String.prototype.replace` with a string pattern, first occurrence only), not a global replace. This is safe only because a surviving `\/` inside a RegExp source is still a literal `/`; `/x\/y\/z/` matches `x/y/z` correctly despite only the first pair being rewritten.
behaviours.pinnedBy: NONE

behaviours.rule: A pattern that fails to compile returns null instead of throwing; the `new RegExp` call is the only statement wrapped in try/catch in the module. No other operation is guarded — `substitute` exceptions and TypeErrors on null input propagate.

formatObligations: `data/regex.json` (profile scope) and `data/shared/regex.json` (shared scope) each hold `{"scripts": [...]}` — a single ordered array, because order is behaviour. Written by writeJsonFile as `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) + "\n"`, UTF-8, mode 0600 (apps/server/src/storage/jsonFile.ts:21-26 via apps/server/src/storage/regex.ts:38-40). Paths: apps/server/src/storage/paths.ts:82-84 (profile) and :129-131 (shared).

On-disk key order per script is the Zod parse order, then passthrough extras appended in input order: `id, scriptName, findRegex, replaceString, trimStrings, placement, disabled, markdownOnly, promptOnly, runOnEdit, substituteRegex, minDepth, maxDepth, <unknown...>`. Verified: a parsed script with `somethingNew` serializes with `somethingNew` last.

A file whose top level is not an object with a `scripts` array reads as an EMPTY list (no throw): `if (!isRecord(raw) || !Array.isArray(raw.scripts)) return [];` (apps/server/src/storage/regex.ts:35-38). A single unparseable script is skipped, not fatal, and the rest of the list still loads (:41-48).

Export download (`GET /api/regex/export`) is a DIFFERENT serialization from the storage file: `JSON.stringify({ scripts }, null, 4)` — 4-space indent — plus a trailing newline, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="catcup-regex.json"` (apps/server/src/routes/regex.ts:51-59).

Import accepts four shapes (apps/server/src/storage/regex.ts:118-134): a bare array of scripts; `{scripts: [...]}`; `{regex: [...]}` (a SillyTavern settings backup); or a single script object recognized by a string `findRegex` OR a string `scriptName`. Anything else imports nothing.

Import assigns ids: keep `record.id` when non-empty else a UUID; a duplicate within the payload gets a fresh UUID; and an id already used in the OTHER scope is replaced with a fresh UUID so a collision cannot hide a rule (apps/server/src/storage/regex.ts:150-184). `mode: 'replace'` only replaces the target scope's list.

`placement` integers are persisted: 0 MD_DISPLAY (retired, kept for round-trip), 1 USER_INPUT, 2 AI_OUTPUT, 3 SLASH_COMMAND, 5 WORLD_INFO, 6 REASONING; 4 is retired and skipped (packages/shared/src/schemas/regex.ts:14-22, docs/DATA-FORMATS.md:676).
`substituteRegex` is persisted as 0/1/2 (NONE/RAW/ESCAPED) and validated by the patch schema as `z.number().int().min(0).max(2)` (packages/shared/src/schemas/regex.ts:25-29, :46, :64).

`minDepth` / `maxDepth` are persisted as `number | null` with default `null` — never as a sentinel like -1 or '' (packages/shared/src/schemas/regex.ts:47-48). The editor converts '' to null on save (apps/web/src/components/RegexSettings.tsx:84-88).

`trimStrings` is persisted as `string[]`; the editor splits the textarea on newlines, trims each line and drops empties, so an empty trim string can only arrive via import, where filterString skips it (packages/shared/src/regex.ts:144; apps/web/src/components/RegexSettings.tsx:96-99).

The module's OUTPUT is what gets persisted verbatim and is therefore a format obligation: stored `mes` for an AI reply (apps/server/src/routes/generate.ts:126), `extra.reasoning` (:129), group replies (groupGenerate.ts:163, :169), stored user text (generate.ts:251, groupGenerate.ts:398, quickreplies/execute.ts:304), edited messages (chats.ts:240, groups.ts:524), greeting swipes (chats.ts:94, :123; groups.ts:241), and world-info entry content placed in the prompt (prompt/worldInfoTurn.ts:182). Any change to `$N` semantics, trim filtering or the fallbacks silently changes bytes already on disk and in every future chat JSONL.

applyRegexScripts passes the same options object to shouldRunRegexScript and runRegexScript — no test asserts the wiring of `depth` or `substitute` through applyRegexScripts (both tests call it with no options).
shouldRunRegexScript: minDepth/maxDepth values exactly equal to depth (the strict `<` / `>` boundary) — only one side of each boundary is tested.
shouldRunRegexScript depth rails: minDepth -1 and -1.5/-2/NaN/±Infinity, maxDepth -1/NaN/±Infinity being ignored, maxDepth 0 being active.
shouldRunRegexScript negative depth (reachable: assemble.ts:521 yields -1 in continue mode and GroupChatView.tsx:891 yields -1 for the optimistic message).
shouldRunRegexScript empty `placement` array making a script inert; and placement values 0 and 4 passing through the includes check.
shouldRunRegexScript strict `=== true` behaviour with truthy non-booleans for isMarkdown/isPrompt/isEdit (e.g. 1), which inverts the gate vs truthiness.
shouldRunRegexScript with BOTH markdownOnly and promptOnly set (runs in either context, never at source).

The `$N` args-index leak: `$(captures+1)` resolving to the offset and `$(captures+2)` to the whole input string, which is then inserted and trim-filtered. No test pins this, and 'fixing' it would change output for any stored script using a high `$N`.
`$<name>` against a pattern with no named groups; `$<>` and `$<a$1>` staying literal / resolving to ''.
`$&`, `` $` ``, `$'`, `$$`, `$x` and a lone `$` remaining literal in replaceString.
`$00` / `$01` numeric parsing with leading zeros.
A group value containing `$1` not being re-expanded (single-pass expansion).
Trim strings applied to `$0` / `{{match}}` (only a `$1` is tested).
Trim strings matching literally (regex metacharacters not interpreted) and case-sensitively.
An empty or macro-expanding-to-empty trim string being skipped rather than used as a needle.
Trim strings applied across multiple matches of a `g` pattern, with the needle re-substituted per match.
The literal replacement text NOT being trim-filtered (only inserted groups are).

sanitizeRegexMacro's full escaped set: `-`, space, `_`, `#`, `'`, `!`, `"`, `%`, `&`, `=`, `<`, `>`, `,`, `:`, `;`, `@`, backtick, `~` all pass through unchanged; and `\r`, `\t`, `\v`, `\f`, `\0`, backslash, `/` being escaped.
sanitizeRegexMacro throwing on null/undefined.
parseRegexFromString: the empty pattern `//`, disallowed flags (`/a/d`, `/a/v`, `/a/gg`, `/a/0`), leading/trailing whitespace, a trailing newline, and multiple escaped delimiters in one pattern.
parseRegexFromString accepting a `/` preceded by `\\` (escaped backslash) even though it is not escaped.
parseRegexFromString throwing a TypeError on null/undefined input.
parseRegexFromString returning a fresh RegExp per call (no cached instance, so no lastIndex leakage between messages).
substituteRegex NONE not calling `substitute` at all for the pattern; and any out-of-schema value (e.g. 3) behaving as NONE.
The find-pattern `substitute` running before parse validation, so its side effects happen even when the pattern turns out invalid.
The default (identity) substitute leaving macros verbatim when options.substitute is omitted — the browser render path with no character context.
runRegexScript returning the input by reference (identity, not just equality) for disabled / empty findRegex / empty raw / invalid pattern / no match.
The editor preview path: a disabled script previews as unchanged text, and macros are not expanded because no substitute is supplied (RegexSettings.tsx:263).
The duplicated delimiter grammar: packages/shared/src/keywords.ts:6-25 must stay in lockstep with parseRegexFromString; nothing asserts the two agree.

The persisted placement integers (0/1/2/3/5/6, 4 skipped) and substituteRegex integers (0/1/2) as literals — every test goes through the constants, so renumbering is invisible to the suite while rewriting the meaning of every stored file.
